clue.text: Sports club

parts.note: read not as a society of players but as a club, a striking implement, used in a sport

explanation.surface: A plain label for a sporting society.
explanation.definitionFit: The willow implement swung by a batsman is literally a club used for a sport.

clue.text: Sit on the fence with dispute between neighbours, perhaps

definitions.note: describes a thing found between neighbouring gardens, standing for the noun

parts.note: to sit on the fence is to avoid committing oneself, to hedge
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Someone stays neutral while two neighbours quarrel over their boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a loose description rather than a strict synonym: a line of bushes often marks the boundary between neighbours' land.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of shrubs commonly forms the boundary dividing neighbouring properties.

clue.text: Consider changing gear on the way

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the word gear are shifted into a new order

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A driver thinks about shifting gear mid-journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it or think about it, a synonym of consider.

clue.text: It used to be very painful

definitions.meaning: an archaic adverb meaning very or greatly
hurting or tender, as a bruised limb is

explanation.surface: Something once caused great pain but no longer does.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb meant intensely, and the everyday adjective means aching or tender.

clue.text: An ample opportunity? Not a bit of it!

definitions.text: An ample opportunity? Not a bit of it!

parts.words: An ample opportunity? Not a bit of it!
parts.note: a plump or large chance would be a big one, yet the idiom means practically no chance at all

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the suggestion that there is a generous opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The ironic idiom means very little likelihood, though literally it suggests a big, ample prospect.

clue.text: I play-act, badly out of character

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of I play-act are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to overacting in a way that does not suit the role.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is unusual or not typical of someone is out of character.

clue.text: Servant in upset during dinner, perhaps

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the little word in is turned upside down, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A servant is flustered while serving dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a domestic servant, someone doing lowly household work.

clue.text: Fair to put the head in charge

indicators.note: in tells us the leading letter is placed inside the payment

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of the word the

explanation.surface: Organisers of a fair appoint someone to run it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes T from 'the', which goes inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair or bazaar, often held to raise funds.

clue.text: Gave out rapidly, as the drunk did?

definitions.meaning: to recite a list quickly and fluently
a drunk staggers or lurches away, reeling as he leaves

explanation.surface: Someone rattled off something fast, like a tipsy person might.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means recited fluently, and literally describes someone staggering away unsteadily.

clue.text: Subject those people to the ultimate in abuse

parts.note: them is the object pronoun for those people

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its last letter, here of abuse

explanation.surface: An instruction to submit a group to the worst kind of mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Related company takes on new agent

indicators.note: takes on says the company has the next piece attached after it
new signals the letters of agent made over in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A sister firm hires a fresh representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means connected by origin or kinship, so related.

clue.text: Joint league champions?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef from the upper part of the leg, sold as a roasting piece
the team at the head of the table could be called the leading team

explanation.surface: Two clubs share the league title.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a butcher's cut of beef for roasting, and whimsically the leading team in a league.

clue.text: Hesitantly stated a colour and was wrong

parts.note: er is the sound of a speaker hesitating
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled while naming a colour and got it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so the past tense means made a mistake.

clue.text: After direction, City Hall works as it should!

indicators.note: after says the reworked letters come behind the compass point

parts.note: E is the compass direction east

indicators.note: works signals the letters of City Hall are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Following orders, the town council for once behaves properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a morally correct way means behaving as one should, rightly.

clue.text: Date of a battle?

explanation.surface: Someone asks on what day a battle was fought.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an appointment, such as a social date, and also a fight between forces.

clue.text: Yeasty reds drunk in recent times

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of Yeasty reds are staggering out of order

explanation.surface: Cheap fizzy red wines were quaffed lately.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means the recent past, days gone by.

clue.text: Breakdown in deliveries?

parts.note: suggests a failure of the post, but means a cricket statistic summarising the balls a bowler has sent down

explanation.surface: A complaint that the post has stopped arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each ball bowled is a delivery; the bowler's figures (overs, maidens, runs, wickets) break down his deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket scorers summarise a bowler's balls bowled, runs and wickets in a statistical breakdown.

clue.text: Sharing common interests — like football clubs?

definitions.meaning: football teams play in a competition, so they are literally part of one

explanation.surface: Fans are compared to football clubs that share a common cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means allied or conspiring, and literally describes teams belonging to a competition.

clue.text: Island doctor turns up to be imprisoned in Asia, unexpectedly

indicators.note: to be imprisoned means the doctor is locked up inside the other letters
unexpectedly signals the letters of in Asia appear in a surprising order
in a down clue, turns up means the doctor's abbreviation is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A medic arrives on the scene and is unexpectedly jailed in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be imprisoned' looks like a phrase about the doctor's fate, but it is the containment signal; 'in' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large Italian island in the Mediterranean, west of the mainland.

clue.text: Doctor, get up and heal this deathly disease

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of get up and heal are altered in order

explanation.surface: A physician is urged to rise and cure a lethal illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person addressed but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The bubonic pestilence that killed millions in medieval Europe is known by this name.

clue.text: Il Duce turned out to be a mathematician

indicators.note: turned out signals the letters of Il Duce are turned around into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Mussolini, known as Il Duce, is claimed to have become a numbers man.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek geometer wrote the Elements, the founding text of geometry.

clue.text: Get involved in someone else's business?

definitions.text: Get involved in someone else's business?

parts.words: Get involved in someone else's business?
parts.note: sounds like meddling, but describes companies combining their businesses into one

explanation.surface: A nosy person is told off for interfering.
explanation.definitionFit: When two firms combine, each becomes part of the other's business, a corporate amalgamation.

clue.text: Doctor got up and down

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

explanation.surface: A physician rose from bed and then fell back.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being gloomy or sullen, a synonym for low spirits.

clue.text: Organised miracle rescue

indicators.note: organised means the letters of miracle are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A planned escape is so successful it seems miraculous.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim is to recover or save something, such as land from the sea, a synonym of rescue.

clue.text: See what has been written about publicity

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ad is a piece of publicity, an advertisement

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at what the press have written about a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan and take in written words is to look at what has been written.

clue.text: Worried, hastened to receive religious instruction

indicators.note: to receive means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: hared means ran fast, like a hare
RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a British school subject

explanation.surface: An anxious person dashed off to get religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Harried means harassed or pestered, so troubled and worried.

clue.text: Even a dull writer may deliver a kick

definitions.meaning: a writer of mediocre, routine copy
to kick an opponent's shins, as in football

explanation.surface: Even an unexciting author can pack a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a writer of humdrum work, and the verb means to kick roughly.

clue.text: Leave word for the French

parts.note: not leaving a message but the word the French use when taking leave, their farewell

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave a message for some French people.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the French farewell, literally 'to God', meaning goodbye.

clue.text: Must it end in tragedy following extraordinary scenes?

indicators.note: following says the next pieces come after the reworked letters
extraordinary signals the letters of scenes are put into an unusual order
the end in a word is its last letter, here of tragedy

explanation.surface: A theatregoer asks whether wild scenes must lead to a tragic ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must' is the noun, as in 'a must-have'.
explanation.definitionFit: A must is something essential or required, an indispensable need.
